title: KV blockwise scale & bias calibration study for low-bit cache encodings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate blockwise scale-and-bias calibration as a mitigation for reconstruction error when storing KV cache in low-bit encodings (FP8/INT8/INT4). Goal is to find a practical calibration workflow that balances quality, runtime overhead, and GPU memory savings for continuous-batching workloads. Deliver a reproducible experiment harness, per-layer/block calibration heuristics, a candidate runtime calibration module, and a recommended fallback policy for production rollout.
success_criteria: 1) Achieve >=2x effective memory reduction on long-context KV cache without >1.5% relative quality regression on our chat and summarization eval sets vs baseline FP16 cache. 2) End-to-end inference latency overhead from calibration <=5ms per request at P95 under continuous batching. 3) Clear rollout plan + safe fallback for high-error shards.
steps: Design block partitioning strategy (tile sizes: 64,128,256 dims) and candidate calibration transforms (per-block scale only, scale+bias, affine with clipping).
Implement offline calibration harness that computes optimal scale/bias per block using representative prefixes from production-like traces.
Run A/B experiments across model sizes (7B/13B/70B) with simulated continuous batching profiles to measure reconstruction MSE, downstream LM quality (chat/summarization), and memory footprint.
Measure runtime cost of applying calibration during restore/write of KV cache on GPU (CUDA kernels) and CPU fallback costs.
Prototype runtime module that stores compact metadata per block (scale,bias in INT8-packed form) and integrates into cache serialization path.
Define heuristics for per-request fidelity gating (e.g., cohort-specific thresholds, request length heuristics) and a policy for on-the-fly dequant fallback when error budget exceeded.
Prepare a rollout playbook with monitoring (reconstruction error heatmaps, per-route quality metrics, latency tail) and canary criteria.
Write docs + design note and open PR for runtime integration and example benchmark notebooks.
artifacts: PR #1293 - runtime: add blockwise calibration apply/restore hooks
notes: This ticket focuses on the calibration transform itself (scale and optional bias) rather than aggressive non-linear compressors. We prefer simple affine compensation because it is cheap to apply on restore and can be fused with existing KV deserialization. Calibration metadata adds a small storage overhead (~1-3% depending on tile size) but may enable 2-4x reduction in raw cache bytes for INT8/INT4 variants.
risks: 1) Calibration mismatch due to distribution shift between offline traces and live traffic could produce visible quality regressions. 2) Per-request runtime overhead could increase latency tail under high concurrency if calibration kernels are not fused. 3) Metadata complexity for many small blocks may negate memory savings.
mitigations: 1) Maintain an adaptive re-calibration window and TTL for stored scales/biases; monitor drift. 2) Implement fused CUDA kernels and fallback to cached fused buffers. 3) Use hybrid tiling (coarse tiles for high-entropy layers, fine tiles for low-entropy layers) to amortize metadata.
preliminary_results: Offline experiments on a 7B decode workload with continuous batching trace: INT8 + per-block scale reduced KV L2 reconstruction error by ~38% relative to symmetric int8 baseline; measured downstream chat BLEU-like quality drop was ~0.9% vs FP16 cache. FP8 + scale+bias matched FP16 within noise for short prefixes but degraded for long-context tails. INT4 shows heavy degradation without bias compensation; blockwise affine improved INT4 reconstruction substantially but still had ~4-6% downstream quality delta on summarization set.
open_questions: What is the minimum viable metadata format (bits per block) we can standardize across runtime, dedicated and private deployments?
Should calibration be computed once offline per model/version or continuously updated in production based on rolling traces?
Can we design a cheap GPU kernel to apply affine restore during KV patching that is memory-bound and fuses with attention KV load to hide latency?
